minimalism_descent: Replaced the ~400-line expected-output synthesizer (_parse_snippet_hunks + _compute_expected_merged + _validator_replacement_key) with 8 small single-purpose functions (largest ~36 lines: _check_hallucinations, _classify_snippet, _merge_is_faithful, _build_segments, _segment_is_faithful, _deletions_justified, _lcs_matched, _real_lines). Instead of synthesizing one mandatory merged output and requiring exact equality, the validator forward-scans the snippet into context anchors + new lines + markers, partitions original and merge into aligned pre/mid/post segments, and checks invariants per segment (new lines land in declared order/multiplicity; survivors keep order/multiplicity via LCS; marker-protected deletions need a unique shared _replacement_key identity or bounded positional adjacency; no-marker gaps are replacement zones). Reuses text_match._replacement_key rather than a second language heuristic. Net -54 lines in chunked_merge.py with no monolithic 175-line section.

The invariant validator intentionally does not pin a marker-inserted new line's exact position relative to surviving originals; it enforces only new-vs-new order, preserved-vs-preserved order, multiplicity, and justified deletions. This surfaced while building the generated matrix (swapping a new line past a survivor inside a marker segment is an allowed placement variant, so the matrix's reorder operator was retargeted to swap two originals, which the validator correctly rejects). This matches the design mandate to validate an allowed set of local outcomes rather than one mandatory merge.

text_match._replacement_key (assignment-LHS only) is exactly the identity deterministic_edit uses for its bug-3 gap-line skip, so reusing it (instead of the removed assign+decl+flow _validator_replacement_key) keeps the validator in parity with the engine and satisfies the no-second-heuristic constraint.
